
I worked this out from the notes and type declarations, not from the library. Setting `beta = -0.5` with no limits set leaves it at -0.5, since nothing clamps it (notes 2, 8). Assuming the usual arc-rotate position formula, the eye lands at (`-10·sin 0.5`, `10·cos 0.5`, 0), which is the same point as `alpha = PI, beta = 0.5`. The view should be upright because the camera has no up-vector field and so uses world +Y. That makes the view identical to the fresh camera.

I'm not sure of three things. The position formula isn't in your notes, so `eyeX` and `eyeY` depend on the usual Babylon convention. The notes don't state that the view uses a fixed world up, so `upright` and `sameAsOtherSide` rest on the absence of an up-vector field in the declarations. And I haven't run anything, so please check the values against `getCameraPosition` once you can run the library.
